reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Monthly billing dispute tickets doubled from ~600 (Jun/Jul 2026) to 1180-1260 (Aug/Sep 2026) (E-01), driven primarily by a defect in the billing import/processing or bill-issuance step that produces incorrect bill amounts independent of read type, as shown by the majority of disputed bills (1785/3025) carrying normal ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED ones (E-04). A field route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, E-05) is a secondary contributor limited to the ESTIMATED-read subset, while tariff changes (E-03) and slow dispute-response handling (E-02) are ruled out as causes.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Monthly billing dispute tickets more than doubled from ~600 (Jun/Jul 2026) to 1180-1260 (Aug/Sep 2026) (E-01), with onset coincident with the 2026-08-01 deployment of validation rule BV-17 (E-13). BV-17 compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), while firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report register values in 0.1 m3 units versus whole m3 units on older v3.x firmware (E-14); this causes legitimate v4.2 readings to be numerically inflated and misflagged as high-consumption, and billing import then rejects these reads (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), accounting for 1184 of the 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads (E-12), which are substituted with estimates and disputed. Tariff changes (E-03) and slow dispute-response handling (E-02) are ruled out as causes. The cause of the remaining majority of disputed bills carrying ACTUAL reads (1785/3025, E-04) is not yet established.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
